question: Not shared. P-331 separates clinician-adjudicated MCI or dementia (NIA-AA 2018, two dementia specialists) from healthy aging in community drivers aged 65-90. The data are three months of passive naturalistic driving, wrist actigraphy sleep and demographics. P-282 separates a psychometric threshold, a Mattis DRS score below 140 ('possible MCI', including mild dementia), from DRS >= 140 in Mayo Clinic Arizona neurology patients aged 21-99 (mean 65.4). The data are eye movements and response times during a one-minute mental-addition task. The measurement channel differs: passive driving and sleep behaviour against task-evoked oculomotor recording (the brief's 'eye or retina' channel), and neither paper uses the other's channel. The label also differs: P-282's authors say the DRS < 140 cut-off captures early cognitive risk rather than established MCI.
metric: Accuracy with accuracy (nominal match). The class mixes differ: 61% impaired in P-331 against 11 of 42 (26%) in P-282's test set, where the majority-class baseline is 31/42 = 0.738.

figures.P-331: Subject-level accuracy from nested LOSO-CV, Model 6: 68.64% = 81/118, Wilson 95% CI [0.598, 0.763].
figures.P-282: Held-out test set of 42 (31 CN / 11 PMCI). The abstract prints accuracy 0.97 for LR with combined time and eye features. Table 5 prints LR-SMOTE accuracy 0.94 [0.88-0.98] at DT = 0.5 and 0.93 [0.88-0.98] at DT = 0.45 (bootstrapped intervals). Wilson check at n = 42: 0.94 gives [0.825, 0.981]; 0.97 gives [0.867, 0.994].

matched_figure_check: No matched figure exists. P-331 reports no eye-tracking or DRS-threshold result, and P-282 reports no driving, sleep or clinician-diagnosis result.
performance_validity: The exclusion applies to the figure the record uses. P-282's headline accuracy of 0.97 is an internal hold-out on 42 people, from a single cohort with no external validation, which meets the Section 3.5 near-ceiling rule. P-282's own Table 5 value for the same model (0.94, CI 0.88-0.98) is below the threshold, so the source is internally inconsistent. P-331's 68.64% is not affected.
reason: The papers measure different channels: passive naturalistic driving and actigraphy sleep in P-331, against eye tracking during a mental-addition task in P-282. They also use different labels (clinician-adjudicated MCI or dementia, against a DRS score below 140 that P-282's authors describe as early risk), so condition 1 fails. The recorded P-282 figure (accuracy 0.97 on a 42-person internal test set with no external cohort) also meets the performance-validity exclusion (condition 5).
